# 004. All pixel art generated by code with a visual review loop

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-11-16

## Context
- The owner decided that all graphics are made by Claude Code, with "the more detailed, the better" (SPEC-REVIEW D-1).
- The previous prototype's art was rejected: sprites were hand-typed text masks drawn "blind" — flat fills, no light, no texture.
- Volume: 15 building types × tiers × 8 lands, characters with many animations.

## Decision
- **Procedural generators** (`assets-src/gen/**/*.ts`) build buildings, terrain, trees, fences, palisade, water, clouds from material primitives (whitewash, reed thatch, logs, planks, shingles, earth rampart), then run passes: directional light (top-left) → material texture → AO → dithering → colored outline → selective outline → **quantize to the master palette** (`assets-src/palettes/master.json`). Tiers, lands and seasons are parameters.
- **Hand-authored indexed masks** (`assets-src/px/*.px`) only for small authored details: faces, hands, costume parts, icons, portraits. Characters are paper-dolls (body + clothing layers + palette swaps), animated by limb offsets.
- **Atmosphere is shader work** in `src/render` (ADR 001), not baked into sprites.
- **Mandatory visual loop:** `pnpm sprites` → `/art-review` screenshots (390×844, dawn / day / golden hour / night) → `art-director` verdict. No ✅ — not merged. The style reference is `docs/art/ART-BIBLE.md`.
- No third-party packs or AI image generation for now; the pipeline still accepts `.aseprite` in case that changes.

## Alternatives considered
- Text masks for everything (prototype approach) — proven to look flat.
- Commissioned artist / licensed packs — rejected by the owner for now; pipeline stays compatible.

## Consequences
- Positive: consistent style, unlimited variations, every asset reviewable and regenerable; atlases rebuilt in CI.
- Negative / trade-offs: generators are real code to maintain; character animation quality is the main risk → validated first in M-ART.
- Follow-ups: ✅ M-ART defined final sizes and ART-BIBLE v1 (ART-20); ✅ palette-compliance check in `build-sprites`.

## Amendment (2026-11-17, M-ART ART-02…19): how the generators actually work
- **Ramp-index buffer space.** Generators never write RGB. `buffer.set(x, y, { ramp, shade, alpha?, material?, normal?, partId?, depth? })` stores a ramp name and a fractional shade; the passes (light top-left → texture → AO → dither → coloured outline → selective outline) work on shades; `quantize` picks the ramp colour and Bayer 4×4-dithers the fractional part. Output is palette-only by construction. Determinism: RNG per frame seeded from `<atlas>:<frame name>`; only `+ − × ÷`, `Math.round`, `Math.sqrt` in output-affecting maths (angles quantized to 1/4096), golden test.
- **Companion masks, not night/shadow sprites.** A generator declares `layers: ['emissive', 'shadow']`; each frame gets same-size companions `<entity>[.<variant>]@emissive/<anim>/<nn>` (windows, openings, lantern, flames; drawn post-grade, ADR 001) and `@shadow` (contact + cast shadow right-down). No separate night sprites.
- **Palette check in `pnpm sprites`** (`tools/lib/sprites/check.ts`): any visible px off `master.json` fails the build; semi-transparent alpha fails outside `SOFT_ALPHA_ATLASES` (`fx`); atlas side ≤ 2048. Two runs must print identical SHA-256 per file. No per-sprite colour-count gate (budget is an ART-BIBLE §4 review rule).
- **Baked whole-px animation instead of runtime filters.** Plant/tree sway (5 lean frames −2…+2 px, whole-px row offsets), windmill sails (8 frames per quarter turn, rasterized per frame) and fire (6 emissive frames) are generated frames; render only picks a frame (`render/sway.ts`, `sailFps`, prop `animate: cycle | sway`). The planned `SwayFilter` and runtime sprite rotation are not used: they resample off the pixel grid.
- **Un-outlined parts.** A part can opt out of the outline pass (e.g. the girl's 1-px ribbons — a coloured outline with a lit side would widen a 1-px strand to 3 px).
- **Paper-doll masks live in the generators**, not in `assets-src/px/*.px`: ASCII masks (`assets-src/gen/lib/doll.ts`, letter = clothing slot + tone, outfit = ramps, outline automatic), shared stamps (`womanStamps`, the Cossack's legs/arms/poses for men), frame tables for limb offsets, palette-swap outfits. A unit test bans outfits that stack white / blue / red bottom-up (SPEC §16). `.px` files stay an option for tiny icons; none exist yet.
- Recipes (`assets-src/gen/lib/recipes*.ts`) are composed with `{ light: false, occlusion: false }` — the recipe places every shade itself; the generic passes are for primitives.
